coaching.headline: A short, brutal mugging. Every Fangtooth, Seedling, the Mini Prime and both towers were ours. They took only river buffs.
coaching.team: Clean fucking work from start to finish. The duo drew first blood, we won all three skirmishes, and our only death came in a trade with Murdock. Their mid barely registered on the damage chart, so this was not a stress test.

focus.title: Every won fight ends in a prize
focus.evidence: All three won fights were followed within 90 seconds by an Outer Tower, Fangtooth or Mini Prime, while the enemy won no fight to convert. The sequence held every time in a short game.
focus.action: After the next won fight, one player names the reachable objective or tower before anyone chases another kill. Next game, check that every won fight is followed by an objective or structure.

perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Xeebs played Feng Mao like the offlane owed him money. Top hero damage in the lobby, kills on both Steel and Scarlett, and zero deaths on a hero where he usually dies plenty. The zero is the impressive part, so treat it as the standard. Next game, when Scarlett is dead or recalling, Feng Mao shoves the offlane wave first, then joins the next Fangtooth or tower call with Earth Shatter ready for whoever is low.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Willy's Belica was the richest player on the map and never died. Facing a Fey who barely dealt damage, he farmed well above his usual pace on the hero and killed Fey and Dekker once each. The gold outran the damage, though, with hero damage under his usual Belica rate. When the mid wave is pushed and Fey is dead or missing, Belica takes that lead to the next fight and opens with Seismic Assault for the team to follow.
perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Goldilocks did the unglamorous shit that ends games early: the heaviest objective damage on our team by a distance, no deaths, and the kill on Scarlett in a won fight. Hero damage was well under his usual Wukong rate, and nobody cares when the pits keep falling our way. Keep that standard: whenever Steel is dead, Wukong starts the next Fangtooth.
perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Proper support work, and it started early. Phase took first blood on Dekker, neither of our duo died in the early lane, and Mr_Meat31 was in on just under half our kills while out-healing everyone in the lobby. Next game, Phase opens fights Linked to Sparrow, who turned fights into bodies here. When Sparrow commits onto Murdock or Dekker, Phase fires Hyperflux in that window so both Phase and Sparrow get the attack speed and haste.
perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Five kills, and both members of their duo went down to Sparrow twice each. When Murdock is still standing in a fight, Sparrow shoots from behind Feng Mao and saves Heightened Senses to slip out once Murdock commits. Cuban Noobster was the finisher, and the only death was a straight swap with Murdock. Damage ran around half his usual Sparrow rate, which is fine when fights end this fast and a problem in a game that drags.

10.7.call: Won 2-0, Sparrow and Feng Mao credited with Steel and Scarlett. Our first Fangtooth fell just before and their first Outer Tower followed. The timing does not show who was at the pit or who hit the tower.

13.5.call: Won 2-0: Wukong took Scarlett and Sparrow took Murdock while they collected a River buff in the same window. Kill credits do not show where the fight happened or who else was nearby.

14.7.call: Won 2-1. Sparrow took Dekker and Murdock and died to Murdock in the same exchange; their second Outer Tower fell, then Fangtooth and Mini Prime. The record does not show who took each prize or whether the death was avoidable.

matchup: Steel died twice and dealt little hero damage; the gank targets mattered more.
Scarlett led their hero damage and Murdock roots; Wukong's credited kill was on Scarlett.
build: Manta Scythe fits a clearing and objectives game, and Wukong had the heaviest objective damage on our team.
It was his only completed item, so the match tested the first purchase, not a full build.
eternal: Lotus grows with time and fights; Immaculate suits entering a gank or pit healthy.
Early Bloom's threshold may not have been reached in a game this short.
Masterpiece is the draft alternative to Early Bloom, trading away the bonus level.
augment: Masterful Mimicry keeps clones coming, supporting overwhelming a target or a pit.
Prosperous Path is the alternative for a snowball game; nothing proves it would have done more.
crest: Nex rewards finishing a gank after damage has landed, not opening one cold.
Hero damage well under his usual rate gives Sow less to store overall.
improvement: Keep Manta Scythe as the farming opener.
Syonic Echo suits Wukong's ability-then-basic rhythm in longer fights; Infernum answers Steel as the body in the way.

matchup: Both enemy duo players immobilize: Dekker's Stasis Bomb with Dynamo, and Murdock's Static Trap.
Phase took first blood on Dekker, and neither of our duo died early.
build: Prophecy pays when Phase can attack safely, and their duo dying six times gave her openings.
Nothing shows Prophecy cost a fight, so no build impact is proven.
eternal: Lotus and Flawless fit an ability-driven healer involved in just under half our kills.
Prima Donna's downside never showed since she did not die, but that does not prove it is safe.
Immaculate is the defensive draft alternative if Dekker's stun lands on Phase first.
augment: Psychic Support pays when the Linked carry runs dry, which the record cannot show.
Kindred Surge is more direct if Murdock's trap or Dekker's stun catches the duo.
With no early duo deaths, there is no case for a forced change.
crest: Phase led the lobby in healing, though Grace's share is not recorded.
The extra ward capacity is there if a longer game needs more coverage.
improvement: Marshal moves Prophecy's value onto allies, suiting a team where Sparrow and Feng Mao did the killing.
Enra's Blessing directly answers Stasis Bomb, Static Trap and Dynamo.
This stomp proves neither swap necessary; choose by whether attack time or lockdown is the problem.

matchup: Sparrow has no dash in her kit, so Murdock's root and Dekker's stun are the real threat.
She killed Murdock and Dekker twice each; her only death traded with Murdock.
build: Lightning Hawk and Vanquisher reward finishing targets, and Sparrow finished plenty.
The common winning core is Storm Breaker, Sky Splitter and Spectra; this short game does not prove either route better.
eternal: Weald, Forage and Wind-Rider make a coherent finisher loadout.
Taproot is the alternative to Wind-Rider when Sparrow needs on-hit healing for longer trades.
augment: Endless Hunt is the right kind of augment in a snowball game, with six takedowns as triggers.
Inner Fury is the teamfight alternative at the cost of the reset engine; nothing here argues for it.
crest: Pacifier is Sparrow's only dash: both her finishing tool and her emergency exit.
Spending it forward leaves Heightened Senses as the only way out.
improvement: Keep the finishing package; five kills and one death give no reason to change it.
If Steel's frontline starts absorbing Sparrow's damage in a longer game, Sky Splitter's current-health damage answers that better than more execute.
If lockdown becomes the problem, Absolution adds tenacity and magical armor, sacrificing some damage; this match tested neither.

matchup: The Fey dealt almost no hero damage all game; the mid threat never showed up.
Scarlett and Dekker did most of their damage, and Steel was the frontline body.
build: Combustion and Wraith Leggings are two pieces of the common winning core.
On core, nothing to teach here.
eternal: Aion's casting mana regeneration supports Runic Focus.
Bottomless Vial only pays for river buffs Belica kills personally, which the record does not show.
Perfection is the slot-two alternative, giving ability haste while healthy instead of mana-scaled power.
augment: Combat Veteran fits a farm-and-rotate mid, though it cannot be credited for Belica's farm.
Against a low-damage mid opponent faster levels are sensible to keep; Devastating Bombs suits a picks plan.
crest: Soulbearer's shield is the right insurance for an immobile mage against Dekker's stun and Murdock's snipe.
Belica took the least damage on our team and never died.
improvement: Noxia, the next winning core item, turns strong farm into more damage, since hero damage ran under his usual rate on Belica.
Seismic Assault into Void Bomb is the natural trigger.
If magical burst from Dekker becomes the threat, Spellbreaker's spell shield is the defensive alternative at the cost of raw power.

matchup: Scarlett was their highest hero damage, with Mutilator omnivamp and a slowing eruption.
Feng Mao had the top hero damage in the lobby without dying; Steel punishes anyone he immobilizes on a dive.
build: Manta Scythe and Omen are the first two items of the common winning core.
Omen brings Reaping Dash and Safeguard back sooner, suiting Feng Mao's dash-and-execute pattern.
eternal: Marrow, Leech and Roses reward exactly what Feng Mao did: stay in fights and finish them.
Leech does not touch Scarlett's Mutilator omnivamp.
Blood Bank is the slot-one alternative for longer trades.
augment: Ichorous Glaive turns an Earth Shatter execution into sustain for the next target.
Seismic Smash is the engage alternative when the team lacks lockdown; Belica's knockup already covered some.
crest: Ortus suits a diver who chains takedowns, and Feng Mao had three.
improvement: Stay on this path: The Perforator completes the common core and helps against Steel's frontline.
If Dekker's magical damage ends dives, Dread trades some offense for magical armor.
Zero deaths says that problem did not appear in this match.

synergy: Our engage/CC: Lt. Belica Neural Disruptor (silence 0.5s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Phase) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Windsurge engage → Cyclebreaker damage-reduction spin → clones from 84000 Hairs
ourKits.winCondition: stance-dance for damage or tankiness and overwhelm with clones
ourKits.playWith: a team that fights alongside his clones
ourKits.playAgainst: AoE clears his clones; CC him during the damage-reduction window

ourKits.combo: Telekinetic Link an ally → Psychic Flare blind → Energy Lance → Hyperflux buff ult
ourKits.winCondition: buff a hyper-carry through the Link and Hyperflux for a teamfight
ourKits.passive: abilities heal her and her linked ally
ourKits.playWith: the strongest carry to Link and supercharge
ourKits.playAgainst: kill the linked carry, not Phase; break the link timing

ourKits.combo: Piercing Shot poke → Heightened Senses AS → Hail of Arrows zone → Inner Fire ult
ourKits.winCondition: ramp Relentless + AS and sustained-DPS the front down
ourKits.playWith: heavy peel — she's immobile and pure DPS
ourKits.playAgainst: she has zero escape — hard-engage her and she dies first

ourKits.combo: Seismic Assault knockup → Void Bomb → Neural Disruptor silence ult, Void Drone mana drain
ourKits.winCondition: knock up + silence a target and burst with missing-HP scaling
ourKits.playAgainst: dodge Seismic Assault; she's immobile — dive when ult is down

ourKits.combo: Reaping Dash → Hamstring slows → Safeguard spellshield → Earth Shatter execute
ourKits.winCondition: trade with the spellshield up and execute low targets with Earth Shatter
ourKits.passive: permanent power on unique hero takedowns
ourKits.playWith: setup that holds a target for the execute
ourKits.playAgainst: bait Safeguard's spellshield before committing the key CC

enemyKits.combo: Bramble Patch slow → Harvest Nettles stacks → Untamed Growth DoT → Fly Trap pull ult
enemyKits.winCondition: Fly Trap a clumped team and detonate AoE on the pull
enemyKits.passive: takedowns spawn growths + grant move speed
enemyKits.playWith: engage that clumps for her Fly Trap
enemyKits.playAgainst: spread out vs the pull; she's squishy — dive her

enemyKits.combo: Bull Rush knockback → Force Shield wall → Shield Slam knockup+stun ult, Shield Bash %hp
enemyKits.winCondition: peel the carry with walls/knockups or engage with Shield Slam

enemyKits.playAgainst: his Force Shield blocks projectiles — reposition around it; bait Shield Slam

enemyKits.combo: Static Trap root → Buckshot → Hot Pursuit AS → Long Arm of the Law global snipe
enemyKits.winCondition: trap for the root, then out-range with Shots Fired and finish with the global ult
enemyKits.passive: every 5th basic is a long-range bonus shot
enemyKits.playWith: frontline/peel to protect his low mobility
enemyKits.playAgainst: almost no escape — engage past the trap and he dies

enemyKits.combo: Stasis Bomb stun → Photon Disruptor slow → Containment Fence wall → Ion Strike slow ult
enemyKits.winCondition: lock a target with stun + fence and let the team collapse
enemyKits.passive: Rocket Boots mobility, refreshed by abilities
enemyKits.playWith: burst that converts her stun/fence into a kill
enemyKits.playAgainst: dodge Stasis Bomb; the fence zones — flank around it
